authorization.quote: accept and integrate, but we must pause before LL21 to tackle another problem
authorization.provenance: User to Codex after Claude audit 116; pause LL21 for browser-portable runtime digest binding.

scope: Accept reviewed S1-LL18-b strong EQ backing-vector movement, at its declared scope.
exclusions: Scanner integration is a shared-runtime change, bound byte-for-byte to the reviewed derived collector and retained for follow-up review.
Native trace answers are also checked against a Python identity map; relocation, cache and generated calling forms are the substantive qualification.
The retained trace expects movement when nonempty because it always has heap keys. Audit 116 independently exercised immediate-only keys; the implementation marks only bucket-key relocation.
The packet options hash_seed is an unused bookkeeping value; the C hash uses a fixed address-word mix.
Growth, weak tables, the HASH-TABLE wrapper, pinned image inventory and production installation remain out of scope. No performance claim.
Only strong EQ vectors; weak, frozen and other hash-vector flags refuse collection.
Capacity is a power of two from 4 through 16384; full insertion is a checked refusal. Automatic table growth is not implemented.
No MAKE-HASH-TABLE, GETHASH or SETF source rewrite is added; generated code reaches the implemented operations through ordinary function values.
No native CLOS HASH-TABLE wrapper, user hash tests, iteration order, weak semantics, cross-Worker sharing or pinned hash-vector inventory is claimed.
The hand-built adapters are internal B leaves, not public host entries or lazy-loader catalog modules. Invalid runtime arguments use checked refusals, not Lisp conditions.
No performance claim. Cache hits and ordinary bucket probes stay in Wasm; a rehash uses owner scratch and runs without a safepoint.
